note: The table carries 133 rows: the 114 NFRx.y DEFINED by this unit plus 19 carried with status N/A because they are CITED by this unit's requirements and DEFINED by an earlier unit -- the same treatment D3 gave its seven inherited ids. Each N/A row names where it comes from and why this design does not discharge it; five of the nineteen (NFR10.15, NFR19.21, NFR19.25, NFR20.17, NFR2.5) appear only inside the ID-disambiguation banner, and their notes say so rather than implying a substantive citation. NFR5.1 is an INCEPTION requirement of the prior record, not a unit-stage id. The 114 are enumerated mechanically by matching the nfr-requirements files, enumerated mechanically by matching the "**NFRx.y** --" definition form rather than transcribed, then checked so that every id APPEARS IN THE PROSE of the design document its target names. D4 MINTS NO NEW ID: a bare NFR6.39, NFR20.16, NFR25.9 or NFR14.41 in a design body is a CITATION of a prior unit's requirement. The BRx.y rows under business_rules are the 41 functional-design rules whose mechanism this stage designs; they are cited, not defined. Four designs carry this unit. (1) The THREE concurrency mechanisms are designed in three separate subsections with a mapping table, because blurring replay (client_mutation_id), conflict (attendance_version) and duplicate generation (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) is the failure that invites the wrong one being reached for. (2) The four-state device queue, whose storage remains the human's choice: every property is designed against behaviour, and reliability-design section 3.7 states the complete delta under Room. (3) The probe matrix, which copies the built four-route shape in tests/privacy/test_profile_probes.py rather than inventing one, including its positive cases. (4) The refusal ordering, where ATTENDANCE_VERSION_CONFLICT carries the roster in error.details and must therefore be unreachable before authorization -- and which the built oracle test CANNOT catch, because that test guards AUTH_403_CODES and this code is a 409. PU-3.6 carries NO performance obligation in V1 [Q14.3 answer C], so no latency mechanism, timing budget or benchmark harness is designed; performance-design section 1 designs the structural replacement and states the absence as the requirement. No test suite could be EXECUTED at this stage: Docker is unavailable in the session, so every claim about built code is from reading the file and is cited by path.
